title: Error E-101: paper feed failure
body: The PX series reports error E-101 when the paper feed motor turns but no sheet arrives from the tray. Fan the paper stack, reload the tray, and confirm the side guides sit snug against the stack. If E-101 returns after reloading, the pickup roller is likely glazed and should be replaced.

title: Error E-210: scanner lamp fault
body: Error E-210 appears on the PX-410 multifunction when the scanner lamp fails to reach full brightness during warm-up. Power the unit off, wait thirty seconds, and power it back on. If E-210 persists across restarts, the scanner assembly requires service.

title: Error E-341: fuser temperature fault
body: Error E-341 means the fuser did not reach operating temperature within the expected warm-up window. Power the printer off, wait ten minutes for the fuser to cool, then restart. If E-341 appears again after the cool-down cycle, the fuser assembly has failed and must be replaced.

title: Error E-342: fuser fan fault
body: Error E-342 indicates the cooling fan next to the fuser is spinning below its rated speed. Check the vent on the rear panel for dust and clear it with a dry cloth. If E-342 remains after cleaning the vent, the fan module needs replacement.

title: Error E-350: fuser thermistor fault
body: Error E-350 is raised when the thermistor that measures fuser temperature returns readings outside the valid range. This is a hardware fault rather than a condition you can clear from the panel. Record the error code and contact service with your serial number.

title: Error E-401: duplex unit fault
body: Error E-401 means the printer cannot communicate with the duplex unit. Power off, remove the duplex unit from the rear of the printer, reseat it firmly until both latches click, and power back on. E-401 usually clears after the unit is reseated.

title: Error E-520: toner supply sensor fault
body: Error E-520 indicates the sensor that tracks toner supply is reporting inconsistent values. Remove the cartridge, wipe the sensor window on the right side of the cavity with a dry lint-free cloth, and reinstall. If E-520 continues, try a different cartridge before scheduling service.

title: Error E-521: drum position sensor fault
body: Error E-521 appears when the drum position sensor cannot detect the drum reference mark. Remove and reseat the drum, checking that the green handle is fully lowered. A drum seated at an angle is the most common cause of E-521.

title: Error E-610: memory fault
body: Error E-610 signals a failed self-test of the printer's internal memory. Disconnect the power cord, wait one minute, and reconnect. If E-610 survives a full power cycle, the main board must be serviced. Print jobs are not stored, so no data is at risk.

title: Error E-704: network module fault
body: Error E-704 means the network module failed to initialize at startup. Restart the printer with the network cable disconnected, then reconnect the cable once the ready screen appears. If E-704 comes back on every startup, update the firmware before calling service.

title: Drum unit DR-4410: when and how to replace
body: The DR-4410 drum unit fits the PX-220 and PX-410 and is rated for twelve thousand pages. To replace it, open the front cover, lift the drum out by the green handle, unpack the new DR-4410, and lower it in until the handle locks flat. Dispose of the old drum through the recycling program.

title: Toner cartridge TN-2210: standard yield
body: The TN-2210 is the standard yield toner cartridge for the PX-220, rated for one thousand two hundred pages. Unpack the TN-2210, shake it horizontally five or six times to distribute the toner, remove the protective seal, and slide it into the drum unit until it clicks.

title: Toner cartridge TN-2211: high yield
body: The TN-2211 is the high yield toner cartridge for the PX-220 and PX-410, rated for three thousand pages. It installs the same way as the standard cartridge and requires no settings change. The panel reads the capacity automatically when the TN-2211 is inserted.

title: Fuser assembly FA-7700: replacement guide
body: The FA-7700 fuser assembly fits all PX series models. Power off and allow one hour of cooling before you begin, because the fuser runs hot. Remove the rear panel screws, disconnect the two keyed connectors, slide the old assembly out along the rails, and fit the FA-7700 in reverse order.

title: Transfer belt TB-3300 for the PX-410
body: The TB-3300 transfer belt is a PX-410 part, rated for fifty thousand pages. Open the top cover, remove all four cartridges, lift the belt unit out by the blue handles, and set the new TB-3300 down flat before reinstalling the cartridges. Never touch the belt surface itself.

title: Pickup roller kit PR-1150: installation
body: The PR-1150 kit contains the pickup roller and separation pad for all PX series trays. Remove the paper tray, release the roller clip inside the feed slot, swap in the new roller, and press the pad into its seat. Replace the PR-1150 parts together so the feed surfaces wear evenly.

title: Fixing streaky or faded output
body: Vertical streaks or faded regions of low toner density usually trace back to the drum. Open the front cover, remove the drum unit, and rock it gently from side to side to redistribute the remaining toner. If the streaks persist on the next print, the drum has reached the end of its life and should be replaced.

title: Ghosting: a repeated image further down the page
body: Ghosting is a dim residual duplicate of the printed image recurring lower on the same page, offset by the circumference of the drum. It means the drum surface is not being cleared between rotations. Replace the drum unit; adjusting density settings will not remove ghosting.

title: Connecting the printer to a wireless network
body: From the control panel, open Network Settings and choose Wireless Setup Wizard. Select your network name from the list and enter the passphrase using the arrow keys. The wireless indicator turns solid blue when the printer has joined the network, and a confirmation sheet prints automatically.

title: Documents wait in the print queue and never print
body: When submitted documents accumulate in the queue but the printer stays idle, the spooler service on the computer has usually stalled. Restart the spooler service, or reboot the computer, then resume the queue. Check also that the printer is not paused or set to offline mode in the operating system.

title: Clearing a paper jam in the rear door
body: When a jam is reported at the rear door, power the printer off before reaching in. Open the rear door, grip the trapped paper with both hands, and pull it out slowly in the direction of the paper path to avoid tearing. Inspect for torn fragments before closing the door and resuming.

title: Pages print blank
body: If every page emerges with nothing printed on it, first confirm the protective seal was removed from the toner cartridge. Next remove the cartridge and shake it horizontally to redistribute toner. Blank pages after both checks indicate a failed developer roller, which requires service.

title: Toner smears under light pressure
body: If printed text smears when brushed with a finger, the fuser is not bonding toner to the paper at full temperature. Confirm the paper type setting matches the loaded paper, since thick stock needs a hotter fusing mode. If smearing continues on plain paper, the fuser assembly is failing.

title: Two-sided printing with the duplex unit
body: The PX series prints two-sided automatically when the duplex unit is fitted. In the print dialog, enable the two-sided option and choose long-edge binding for documents read like a book. Use paper in the supported weight range, since heavy stock cannot travel the duplex path.

title: Long delay before the first page
body: A long pause before the first page emerges is usually the fuser warming from deep sleep, which can take up to twenty seconds. Shorten the sleep timer if the delay bothers you, or raise it to save energy. Large documents can also delay the first page while the job is processed.

title: Creased or wrinkled output
body: Wrinkled or creased pages usually mean the paper absorbed moisture. Load a fresh ream that has been stored flat in its wrapper, and confirm the tray guides are snug so the sheet feeds straight. Persistent creasing on fresh paper points to a worn exit roller.

title: Gray background on printed pages
body: A light gray tint across areas that should be clean paper means the drum is charging unevenly or the density is set too high. Lower the print density one step in the panel menu, and clean the corona wire. A drum near the end of its rated life also produces background tint.

title: Wireless connection drops repeatedly
body: If the printer joins the network but loses the connection during the day, assign it a static address on the router so the lease cannot expire mid-job. Keep the printer away from microwave ovens and thick walls, and prefer the two point four gigahertz band for range.

title: Printing envelopes from the multipurpose slot
body: Feed envelopes one at a time through the multipurpose slot at the front, flap side down. Set the media type to envelope in the print dialog so the fuser uses the cooler envelope mode. Expect minor wrinkling on cheap envelopes; heavier stock feeds more reliably.

title: Setting up scan to email on the PX-410
body: Scan to email sends scanned documents directly from the PX-410 to a recipient address. In the web console, enter your outgoing mail server, port, and account credentials under Scan Settings, then register recipient addresses in the address book. Scans are sent as searchable PDF attachments.

title: Toner low warning: what it means
body: The toner low warning appears well before the cartridge is empty, typically with fifteen percent remaining. Printing continues unaffected until the replace toner message appears. To squeeze out the last pages, remove the cartridge and shake it horizontally, which levels the remaining toner.

title: Enabling quiet mode
body: Quiet mode halves the motor speed to cut noise roughly in half, at the cost of slower printing. Enable it from the panel under General Settings, or on a schedule so overnight jobs run silently. Quiet mode does not change print quality, only speed and noise.

title: Installing the print driver on macOS
body: Download the macOS driver package from the support site and open the installer. When the installer finishes, add the printer under System Settings, where it appears with a Bonjour label. The driver enables the two-sided option, tray selection, and toner level display.

title: Installing the print driver on Windows
body: Download the Windows driver package from the support site and run the installer as administrator. Choose the connection type when prompted, either the network option or the supplied cable. The installer registers the printer and applies the recommended defaults for the region.

title: Updating the printer firmware
body: Firmware updates fix paper handling faults and network issues, so apply them when offered. From the web console, open Maintenance and choose Firmware Update; the printer downloads the image, verifies it, and restarts itself. Never power off during a firmware update, since an interrupted write can disable the printer.

title: Printing from a phone or tablet
body: The PX series accepts jobs from phones and tablets over the standard mobile printing services built into the operating system. Both the printer and the mobile device must be on the same network. No app installation is required; the printer appears in the share sheet automatically.

title: Colors look wrong on the PX-410
body: When printed colors drift from what the screen shows, run the automatic color calibration under Maintenance in the panel menu. Calibration takes about two minutes and realigns the four cartridges. Run it after replacing any cartridge or moving the printer, and expect a calibration page to print.

title: Printing on label sheets
body: Use only label sheets rated for laser printers, and feed them through the multipurpose slot to keep the paper path straight. Set the media type to labels so the fuser runs in its cooler mode. Never reuse a sheet with labels already peeled off, because exposed adhesive can wrap the fuser.

title: Cleaning the corona wire
body: The corona wire charges the drum, and toner dust on the wire causes streaks and background tint. Open the front cover, find the green slider on top of the drum unit, and move it fully across and back several times. Return the slider to its home position, or a dark vertical line will appear on every page.

title: Paper size mismatch message
body: A size mismatch message means the size in the print job differs from the size configured for the tray. Set the tray size in the panel menu to match the loaded paper, and check the document's page setup. The regional default differs between markets, which is the usual cause after a move.

title: Registering your printer for warranty coverage
body: Register within sixty days of purchase to activate the full two year warranty. You will need the serial number from the label inside the front cover and your proof of purchase. Registration also enrolls the printer for firmware notices and recall bulletins.

title: Recycling used cartridges and drums
body: Every new cartridge and drum ships with a prepaid return label in the box. Place the used part in the packaging the new one arrived in, apply the label, and drop it at any parcel point. Returned parts are remanufactured, and nothing goes to landfill.

title: Restoring factory default settings
body: A factory reset clears network settings, the address book, and all menu customizations. From the panel, open General Settings, choose Reset, and confirm with the serial number's last four digits. The printer restarts with the out-of-box configuration and prints a settings summary.

title: Changing the display language
body: The panel language is set independently of the driver language. Open General Settings, choose Display Language, and select from the fourteen supported languages. The change applies immediately without a restart and does not affect printed reports.

title: Adjusting the sleep timer
body: The printer enters deep sleep after a period of inactivity, five minutes by default, drawing under one watt. Lengthen or shorten the timer under General Settings. Waking from deep sleep takes several seconds while the fuser reheats, which is the tradeoff for the energy savings.

title: Paper storage and humidity
body: Store paper flat in its original wrapper until the day you load it, in the same room as the printer where possible. Paper that absorbs ambient moisture curls, feeds badly, and fuses poorly. In humid climates, load only what the tray will consume in a day.

title: Contacting support and finding your serial number
body: Before contacting support, note the model name, the serial number from the label inside the front cover, and any error code shown on the panel. Support can remotely read the printer's event log if you enable the assistance option in the web console during the call.

title: Ordering genuine supplies
body: Order supplies through the web console's supplies page, which knows your model and lists only compatible items. Genuine supplies carry a hologram seal on the box. Third party refills are not covered by the warranty, and damage they cause is billed even during the warranty period.
